title: DeliveryDefectTaskRequest
description: Body of `POST /delivery/v1/defect-tasks` (v0.59.0): ask the `youtrack` service to create one defect task under an epic after an epic-level test found a problem. `operationKey` is the idempotency key (same grammar as the `{operationKey}` path parameter of the operations routes): the same key with the same canonical body replays the stored answer (`200`); a different body under the same key is `409 operation_key_conflict`. The `delivery.sync-request` payload kinds stay closed at link, comment, transition and resolve; creating an issue is not one of them, which is why this operation has its own route. Additive (D043): nothing existing changes; a consumer pins the release that introduces this schema before it calls the route.

operationKey.description: Idempotency key chosen by the caller.

epic.description: The epic the defect task belongs to. The service refuses a reference that is not an epic (`not_an_epic`) or whose live `vendorId`/`idReadable` pair differs (`epic_mismatch`).

outcome.description: What must be true once the defect is fixed. At most three sentences (a producer rule; a schema cannot count sentences).

scope.description: What the task covers, one entry per item.

acceptance.description: Acceptance criteria, one entry per criterion.

source.description: Where the defect came from. Closed to `epic-test`; a new source is an additive change.

note.description: Free-text finding from the epic test, recorded on the new task.
